## Correlation patterns

A correlation pattern groups related alerts into a single incident.

### Editing a pattern

You can edit a correlation pattern at any time from the **Correlation** page.

> **Note:** Changes to a pattern apply only to new alerts. Existing incidents keep their current grouping until they are resolved.

## Maintenance Plans

Use a maintenance plan to suppress alerts during planned work.

### Prerequisites

- You must have **Admin** permissions to create or edit a maintenance plan.

### Create a Maintenance Plan

1. Create the maintenance plan.
2. Save the plan.

After you save the plan, it appears in the maintenance plan list.

> **Tip:** Notify your team before the plan starts.

### Stop a Maintenance Plan Early

You can stop an active maintenance plan before its scheduled end time.

## Troubleshooting a failed sync

If a sync fails, check the integration logs to identify the cause.

### Expired token

An expired token is the most common cause of sync failures. To resolve it:

1. Generate a new token.
2. Paste the new token into the **Token** field.

The sync resumes automatically. You don't need to restart the integration.

### Failure in a single environment

If the failure affects only one environment, re-run the sync for that environment only.

To send a test alert, run the following command: <!-- [VERIFY: confirm the default port with engineering] -->

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/alerts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{"status": "critical", "host": "db-01"}'
```

Replace `<your_api_key>` with your API key.

> **Note:** The alert can take up to 30 seconds to appear.
